content.title: Jazz vs. Nuggets: Prediction, How to Watch for Free (3/27/26)
content.text: The Utah Jazz (21–52) face the Denver Nuggets (46–28) tonight at Ball Arena in Denver. The Nuggets enter on a four-game winning streak, defeating the Dallas Mavericks on Wednesday in a 142–135 shootout, led by Jamal Murray, who finished with a season-high 53 points. Nikola Jokic astounded in his own distinct way, posting yet another triple-double, totalling 23 points, 21 rebounds, and 19 assists. Peyton Watson, playing in his second game back from injury, showcased just how valuable he is, scoring 21 points in just 23 minutes. Denver sits in fourth place in the Western Conference, 1.5 games behind the third-place Los Angeles Lakers, with a half-game lead over the Minnesota Timberwolves. The Nuggets are comfortably positioned for an automatic playoff berth, barring an epic collapse in this final stretch of the season. The Jazz, meanwhile, have lost three straight, the worst of which was their 133–110 loss on Wednesday to the Washington Wizards — not because of the margin, but because of the opponent, which entered on a 16-game losing streak. Cody Williams led shorthanded Utah with 24 points and Blake Hinson followed with 21. Rookie Ace Bailey struggled from the floor, shooting just 7-of-19, finishing with 15 points. There was little in the way of defense from Utah, which allowed the Wizards to shoot 55% from the field and dominate the boards, outrebounding the Jazz 56 to 40. Denver’s home-court advantage, offensive efficiency, and depth give them a clear edge against a Utah team struggling defensively. Prediction: Denver Nuggets 121, Utah Jazz 108 Injury Report Utah Jazz Isaiah Collier — Out (Hamstring) Keyonte George — Out (Hamstring) Lauri Markkanen — Out (Hip) Jusuf Nurkic — Out (Nose) Jaren Jackson Jr. — Out (Knee) Walker Kessler — Out (Shoulder) Denver Nuggets No injuries reported. How to Watch Jazz vs. Nuggets Tip-off for tonight’s Jazz-Nuggets game is set for 9:00 PM Eastern / 7:00 PM Mountain at Ball Arena in Denver. The game airs live locally on KJZZ and Altitude Sports. Out-of-market viewers can stream the matchup on NBA League Pass for free on Amazon Prime Video with a 7-day free trial here. Amazon also offers a discounted subscription that starts at $12.74 for the first two months (then $16.99/month). The subscription also includes access to NBA TV. Fans can also choose a Team Pass to follow one team’s games for $13.99 per month.
